42% of the time, the AI model does not matter.

That is not speculation. Stanford researchers studied 51 real enterprise AI deployments across seven countries, nine industries, and 14 business functions. In nearly half the cases, the specific AI model used was considered completely interchangeable.

The actual obstacles to success were human and structural: redesigning processes, building trust across teams, getting organizational buy-in, and constructing the data infrastructure to make AI work at scale.

This is the uncomfortable truth most AI conversations skip. Executives spend months evaluating models while the real blockers — culture, data, and operational design — go unaddressed.

The flagship model race between OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and xAI is producing increasingly capable technology on rapid cycles. But capability without execution is just a demo.

The organizations pulling ahead are the ones treating AI as an operating model challenge, not a technology procurement decision.
